title: Periodic Table and Properties - Chemistry - Electron Affinity
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Electron Affinity is defined as the energy change when:
options: An electron is removed from a gaseous atom
An electron is added to a gaseous atom
An atom transitions from solid to gas
questions.explain: Electron Affinity is the energy change (usually release) when a neutral gaseous atom gains an electron to form an anion.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which element has the **most negative** (highest magnitude) Electron Affinity?
questions.explain: While Fluorine is more electronegative, **Chlorine** has the highest electron affinity. Fluorine's very small size leads to inter-electronic repulsion when an electron is added, making it less favorable than adding one to the larger Chlorine atom.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why do Noble Gases (Group 18) have positive Electron Affinity values?
options: They have high effective nuclear charge
They have stable, fully filled shells and must absorb energy to accept an electron
They are gases at room temperature
They have very low ionization energies
questions.explain: Noble gases have a full valence shell ($ns^2 np^6$). Any added electron must go into a higher energy principal shell ($n+1$), which is energetically unfavorable, requiring energy input (endothermic).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which group of elements generally exhibits the most exothermic (negative) electron affinities?
questions.explain: Halogens have an $ns^2 np^5$ configuration. They are one electron short of a stable octet, so gaining an electron releases a large amount of energy.
questions.subject: Chemistry
